idiom_name: shared frozen object literal with benign methods; Proxy with a catch-all get trap
implementation_notes: JavaScript needs no hierarchy at all: a shared object literal that exposes the same method names with benign bodies is the special case, and Object.freeze keeps it from being mutated accidentally. Where the interface cannot be enumerated in advance - a third-party tracker, a plugin host - a Proxy whose get trap returns a no-op function (chained back to the proxy) absorbs every call. A subclass is only worth it when instanceof or class identity is part of the contract. The `noop` function exported by many libraries, and Node's habit of accepting an empty object for optional collaborators, are the same idea in the ecosystem.
pitfalls: A Proxy swallows typos and API drift: mistyped methods silently exist, so the technique can hide integration errors instead of surfacing them.

Identity checks only work if one instance is shared - `x === nullLogger` - while instanceof fails for object literals and behaves differently for proxies, which do not forward native internal slots (Map, Date) or private fields.
Object.freeze is shallow: nested arrays and objects inside the special case stay mutable.
A no-op that returns undefined breaks chained callers that expect a value or a fluent object; decide what 'do nothing' returns per method.
